note: Lab-measured FODMAP components (g per 100 g as eaten/as sold) from open-access full texts read this session via Europe PMC/NCBI (Chumpitazi 2018 J Pediatr Table 1 — US foods, Megazyme kits; Ferjančič 2024 Front Nutr Table 1 — total fructan in Slovenian foods; Matias 2024 Plant Foods Hum Nutr Table 1 — Spanish wheat bread group mean; Laatikainen 2016 Aliment Pharmacol Ther Table 1 — regular rye bread; Alghamdi 2020 Saudi J Biol Sci Table 2 — honey sugars; Panseri 2021 Foods Table 4 — milk lactose; Torbica 2025 Foods Tables 2–3 — wheat pasta; Alowo 2025 Front Nutr Tables 2/4 — millet, sorghum, sesame) plus values stated in two abstracts (Whelan 2011 rye bread; Prichard 2016 guava, fenugreek). Each row carries one FODMAP component; 'not detected' is recorded as 0 with the detection limit where stated. Excess fructose is taken as reported or computed as fructose − glucose from the same sample (negative set to 0) and labelled as such. GOS for Torbica = raffinose+stachyose+verbascose summed by us. Torbica fructan rows are short-chain FOS only and are excluded (comparison only). No Monash app/website data used. Monash cutoffs (Varney 2017) were only seen second-hand — see papers.md. Serving sizes from USDA FoodData Central SR Legacy household portions (Cornmeal left null because the value is for cooked polenta). Pico edits: Rye left out (values are rye bread, catalog Rye is the grain); dry grains given a 1/4 cup uncooked serving to match legumes.
